newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees next Eurobond issue in 2-3 months.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees next Eurobond issue in 2-3 months.

text.p: Russia plans to make its second Eurobond issue in two or three months and two more issues will appear in the second half of the year, Interfax news agency quoted a Finance Ministry official as saying on Thursday.
Deputy head of the foreign credits department Vladimir Dmitriyev said the second issue would most likely be in marks, Interfax said.
The third Eurobond issue, no earlier than three months after the second one, will be dollar-denominated and aimed specially at the U.S. market, Interfax quoted Dmitriyev as saying.
This would be followed by yet another issue, the third this year, he said.
The Finance Ministry was also considering a yen-denominated Eurobond, Dmitriyev said.

Russia launched its debut $1.00 billion five-year Eurobond last November. Government officials have said the next issue will be launched in the first quarter of 1997 and Russia planned to raise a total of $1.5 billion in 1997.
